title.narrative: We Effect Inclusive Market-Led Value Chains iMoved 2022-2026
We Effect Inclusive Market-Led Value Chains iMoved 2022-2026

description.narrative:
Goal: To contribute to an inclusive, market-oriented value chain development of the dairy, soya and horticulture sector for sustainable livelihoods and economic empowerment of female, male and youth smallholder farmers in 13 districts of Zimbabwe.
Outcome: Increased income for female, male and young smallholder farmers participating in the dairy, soybeans and horticulture value chains.
The project is organised into five outputs:
- Sustainable and efficient production capacity, including value addition
- Access to and linkages to reliable and economically viable input suppliers and markets for smallholder farmers
- Access to Business Development Services (BDS)
- Enabling environment for dairy, soybeans and horticulture value chain participation
- Strengthened women's participation and leadership in the dairy value chain to reduce institutional and market barriers and promote inclusive economic development for women in dairy.
The project is aiming to reach out to 10 500 direct beneficiaries of which 60 % will be women. The expected outputs or achievements of the project include:
- Household incomes from participation in the three value chains shifts from subsistence to economically viable sectors for households participating in the selected value chains
- 80% of smallholder farmers (60% women) reporting increased income as a result of project supported value chain activities.

The application for support by We Effect titled Inclusive, Market-Oriented Value Chains for Economic Development (iMoved) Project 2022-2026, looks at developing three value chains in the agriculture sector, namely, the dairy, soyabeans and horticulture value chains. The project proposes to reach out to 10 500 beneficiaries, of which 60 % will be women across select 13 districts in Zimbabwe. In considering the decision to approve this support, the Embassy believes that the intervention will contribute to results under the new strategy for Sweden Development Cooperation for Zimbabwe, 2022-2026 across all the three areas of support. While it will mainly contribute to the Inclusive Economic Development thematic area's sub-objectives of sustainable livelihoods, including food security and productive, resilient and sustainable agriculture and improved opportunities for productive employment and decent work, the proposal is very integrated in that it will also contribute results under Gender Equality as well as the sub-objective relating to strengthened resilience to climate change and environmental and natural disasters, greater access to renewable energy and higher energy efficiency under the Environment, Climate and Sustainable use of Natural Resources thematic areas.

We Effects ansökan med titeln ’Inclusive, Market-Oriented Value Chains for Economic Development (iMoved) Project 2022–2026’, har som mål att stödja utvecklingen av tre värdekedjor inom jordbrukssektorn, nämligen värdekedjorna för mejeri, sojabönor och trädgårdsodling. Insatsen kommer att bidra till resultat inom samtliga tre stödområden under den nya strategin för Sveriges utvecklingssamarbete för Zimbabwe, 2022–2026. Projektet riktar sig till runt 10 500 stödmottagare, varav 60 % kvinnor i 13 utvalda distrikt runtom i landet. Till största del bidrar projektet till stödområdet för inkluderande ekonomisk utveckling och delmålet för hållbar försörjning, inklusive livsmedelsförsörjning och produktivt, motståndskraftigt och hållbart jordbruk, förbättrade möjligheter till produktiv sysselsättning samt anständigt arbete. Projektförslaget bidrar även till resultat under stödområdet för jämställdhet samt stödområdet som rör stärkt motståndskraft mot klimatförändringar och miljö- och naturkatastrofer, ökad tillgång till förnybar energi och högre energieffektivitet inom temaområdena miljö, klimat och hållbar användning av naturresurser.

The projects key results for 2024 include: 1. The project managed to contribute to increased milk production for the year with the national milk production reaching to just below 115 million litres per year, an increase on the 2023 milk volumes by 15%. To this national volume the iMoved dairy hubs contributed 1.6% with a total volume of 1.84million litres of milk delivered to the formal markets resulting in USD1,012 million dollars at an average price of USD0,55. The year under review also had Somabhula and Romac dairy hubs making their inaugural milk deliveries to Dairiboard Zimbabwe with annual deliveries of 18,512 and 3,102 litres respectively as a result of the project's support that included inspection and certification of dairy farmers as well as sample collection and testing of raw milk which is are key requirements for dairy participation.
2. The project contributed to the diversification of especially women smallholder farmers' income sources through established 13 green hubs participation in oil pressing, soya and sunflower cake production with an average of USD370 per month per site. This was further strengthened with greenhouse production with 3 sites that started selling their produce making an average of US950.00 per week per site. This has enabled smallholder farmers to contribute to the purchase of dairy animals, participate in dairy breed improvements through artificial insemination utilizing the subsidized semen revolving fund, enhance participation in income savings and lending schemes.
3. The project managed to strengthen access to critical services through engagement of private players along the value chains which resulted in contracts being developed between off takers and smallholder farmers and input suppliers across the value chain. A total of 7 contracts were developed and this included Dairiboard Zimbabwe Limited, FeedMix, Coopers, Fivet, Syngenta, Nyaningwe Supermarket, Local institutions such as boarding schools, hospitals and mines.
4. Number of functional sites: A total of nine agricultural hubs are fully functional with the exception of Datata and Umguza whose dairy value chain is yet to be developed Chikwaka as the soya bean hub is yet to be developed and Somabhula where the green hub development was affected by dry holes.
5. Increased participation of women in leadership positions: The percentage of females in leadership positions across the three value chains improved from 49.3% in 2023 to 52% in 2024. This was mainly due to the trainings that were done in 2024 and influencing of new committees that were being elected in office after their terms of office came to an end during the reporting period. Leaders from successful Internal Savings and Lending groups provided a good base for coaching and mentoring of prospective leaders. A total number of 1,671 women are participating in internal savings and lending clubs in all the project sites a huge increase from 980 women achieved in 2023.
Key results at Output level
* Sustainable and efficient production capacity, including value addition The promotion of sustainable and efficient agricultural practices during the reporting period was advanced through equipping 9 hubs and the introduction of innovative production systems. The assets in the agriculture hubs are benefiting more than 3, 000 rights holders in the 13 sites and these assets resulted in improved production capacity in all three value chains.
Marirangwe serves as a mechanization support under the projects grant and matching grant facilities. iMoved Project extended USD11,000.00 to the Dairy Hub and a further USD7,000.00 through a matching grant facility which the members matched with their own USD7,000.00 bringing the total to USD25,000.00. These funds were used to procure hay baling equipment (bailer, rake and slasher), silage equipment and a tractor drawn trailer as own feed formulation had been identified as the major thrust for the Marirangwe dairy farmers especially after the effects of the 2023/24 drought season. The fodder conserved enabled farmers to maintain their animals in a relatively good body condition score as well as growing the milk volume for Marirangwe despite the drought. These results at output level feed into the main results under which the hub is identified as the best performing in terms of milk production as well as site and household income generation for 2024.
Collaborations with private sector players like Kurima Centre, Easiseeds, Coopers, Fivet, Feedmix, dairy processors, Government technical extension and Zimbabwe Dairy Industry Trust (ZDIT) have improved service provision and capacity building at agriculture hubs. Through these players, farmers knowledge and skills were enhanced in hygienic milk production, animal health, artificial insemination, breed improvement, climate smart farming, feed formulation, infrastructure development, farm management, equipment use and maintenance as well as general animal husbandry.
* Access to and linkages to reliable and economically viable input suppliers and markets for smallholder farmers A total of 454 dairy farmers were reached with marketing information across the iMoved dairy sites during the year 2024 against a target of 1,000. A project specific WhatsApp chat BOT (a communication interface using the WhatsApp platform that farmers can register to be part of, to receive information on the various aspects around production, markets, financial linkages, value addition, service providers and off takers for example) was also finalised during the reporting period. This will be the main platform to be used to link farmers to regular and accurate market and extension related information going forward. The chat bot is housed at ZADF.
A total of 1,343 farmers against an annual target of 3,000 farmers reported improved access to inputs on competitive terms and conditions. This has resulted in the adoption of sunflower and soya beans production as evidenced by an increase in in hectarage planted and number of farmers in the soya/oil value chain across the 13 sites compared to 2023. The roll out of the semen revolving fund for artificial insemination has improved access especially for women and youth smallholder farmers from all 13 project sites who are interested in getting into dairy farming through the beef dairy model.
* Access to Business Development Services (BDS) The project facilitated dialogue meetings between farmers and Business Development Service (BDS) providers that includes both private and public entities. The objective was to improve access to services such as financial, certification, health/extension and marketing as discussions brought out smallholder farmers priorities.
The project facilitated co-creation of models together with private sector players that contributed and strengthened pluralistic extension which bridged the information gap along the value chains. Tailor made services were developed to address low production, productivity and access to markets for both inputs and outputs. For example, the project integrated farmer structures such as ISAL groups, Rural Womens Assemblies (RWAs), study circle groups into the three value chain related hubs. The structured groups became an entry incentive for the private sector in their engagement with smallholder farmers who they have traditionally perceived as not organized for their products.
Further, the project took advantage of the already planned forums that the partners, WLZ and ZADT, by virtue of them being membership based, traditionally use to engage with policy issues. These platforms allowed the members to interact with private and public players and issues that were affecting smallholder farmers were presented as a policy or practice alternative.
* Enabling environment for dairy, soybeans and horticulture value chain participation The project continuously lobbied and advocated for a conducive economic and regulatory environment by building evidence through identification of policy related bottlenecks. For example, project supported women and youth small holder farmers with strategies on how to effectively engage duty bearers and this led to allocation of 5hectare plots and led to increased service provision from government extension officers across the 13 sites. The project sites are in different localities with unique governance structures that have to be followed to access land.
In addition, regards financial products and services, ZB Bank and Zimbabwe Women's Micro finance Bank developed a product for smallholder farmers and carried out farmer assessments. At the end of the reporting period, the two financial institutions were finalizing processing of loans to smallholder farmers at Cynara and Umguza Agricultural Hubs. These loans have been specifically designed for dairy and horticultural farmers and will act as pilot initiatives with the intention of scaling these up to the remaining project sites.
* Strengthened women's participation and leadership in the dairy value chain to reduce institutional and market barriers and promote inclusive economic development for women in dairy. Perceptions from key service providers has always been that women smallholder farmers are risky with limited collateral and this limited expansion of women's economic participation. To caveat that view and bring women up in the sector, the project invested in influencing existing farmer structures to include women in leadership positions so that they advocate for specific issues that affect them. The project also ensured that the Rural Women's Assemblies are established across the 13 project sites to function as a vehicle towards lobbying and advocating for space in the value chains of choice.
